description: THE STAGING FLOW (reddoor-maintenance#545, Operator decisions 113, answered 2026-10-12). Opt-in: a repo extends this AFTER renovate-config, and only once it has a `staging` branch with a ruleset requiring `ci / ci` and a `main-gate` check on `main`. It is not in renovate-config because its rules disable majors on `main`, which on a repo with no `staging` would leave majors with no branch at all.

The operator's rule, verbatim in intent: patches and minors target `main` and fast-track (the automerge rule in renovate-config merges them on green, with no operator PR per update; 'if I have to PR and merge for every patch update it pretty much defeats the point of renovate'). Majors, and every other update type, target `staging`, and reach production only through the operator's promotion PR.

With two base branches Renovate prefixes branch names with the base (`renovate/main-all-minor-patch`, `renovate/staging-sveltejs-kit-3.x`), read from its source (workers/repository/process/index.js, isMultiBaseBranch). A branch that exists under the old name is closed and reopened under the new one on the first run.

`main-gate`, the required check on `main`, lets through a PR from `staging`, or a PR authored by reddoor-renovate[bot] on a `renovate/` branch whose every commit that bot authored and which carries the `fast-track` label added by that bot. The label below is how the gate tells a patch or minor from anything else: only the `main` patch/minor rule adds it, and Renovate unions `addLabels` across a grouped PR's upgrades (workers/repository/updates/generate.js), so a group of patches and minors carries it.

Vulnerability alerts are not bound by these rules: Renovate appends one packageRule per alert with `force: { enabled: true }` (workers/repository/init/vulnerability.js), which overrides `enabled: false`. A security fix that is a patch or minor gets the label and passes the gate; a major security fix into `main` is held by the gate for the operator, who retargets it or merges it on his word.
Lock-file maintenance goes to `staging`: the operator named patches and minors, and a whole-tree refresh is neither.

packageRules.description: On main: only patches and minors.
On staging: everything but patches and minors, which already go to main.
The mark main-gate reads. Only this rule adds it.
